description: Assembler of the hand-written modules src/asm/*.asm (cs [0x6f26,0x9413), between the compiled C and CS.LIB). Driven by tools/asm.py under DOSBox-X; installed into the git-ignored toolchain/ASM/<assembler>/ by tools/bootstrap.py. Evidence reproducible with tools/asm_identify.py --modules.
options_note: Single pass (no /m): TASM 2.0 with /m2 removes the forward-jump NOPs and mismatches both modules (2383 / 3769 differing bytes). /mx (case-sensitive publics, for linking with Turbo C) is not observable in the bytes.

evidence: Forward jumps to near labels are EB xx 90 (cs 747a, 755f, 7568, 75a2, 7979, 7984, 83b7): a one-pass assembler that reserved 3 bytes. Rules out MASM 6.x and TASM /m (multi-pass); consistent with MASM 4/5 and TASM 1.x/2.x single pass.

cs 750a: 9C 0E E8 0A 00 90 = pushf; push cs; call near Int8ISR; nop. Only TASM 2.0 / 2.01 turn a forward `call far ptr` to a procedure in the same segment into PUSH CS / CALL NEAR / NOP; TASM 1.0, 1.01 and MASM 4.0 / 5.0 / 5.1 / 5.1A all emit 9A (far call + base16 fixup, which would also need an MZ relocation at cs 750e that the image does not have).

src/asm/lowlevel.asm and src/asm/tiles.asm are EXACT under TASM 2.0 and under TASM 2.01; lowlevel.asm is MISMATCH under TASM 1.0 and 1.01 (the far call). No construct in the game distinguishes 2.0 from 2.01; 2.0 is pinned as the release contemporary with Turbo C++ 1.0 (May 1990, the pinned compiler), 2.01 being its later bug-fix release.

Both modules start word aligned after a single 00 TLINK pad byte (cs 6f25 after the last C function, cs 7e59 between the modules): _TEXT is WORD aligned, as with TASM .MODEL small (or explicit `segment word`). Their _DATA is also word aligned (pad ds 132d before lowlevel's data, ds 13a9 between the modules, ds 1439 after tiles' data).
Every one of the 14 MZ relocations inside the assembly range (cs 7520 ... 940e) is a `mov ax,DGROUP` base16 fixup of one of the two modules; none is left over.

rejected.name: TASM 1.0 / 1.01
rejected.why: forward `call far ptr` assembles to 9A (5-byte far call with a segment fixup), not 0E E8 xx xx 90 (cs 750a)

rejected.name: MASM 4.0 / 5.0 / 5.1 / 5.10A
rejected.why: same 9A far call; MASM 4.0/5.1/5.10A additionally emit 81 /7 iw for a forward-EQU immediate where TASM and MASM 5.0 emit 83 /7 ib + 90 (probe only, no instance in the game). The sources also use TASM LOCALS (@@ labels).

rejected.name: MASM 6.0
rejected.why: not run (ML needs its DOS extender); it optimizes jump lengths, so it cannot produce the EB xx 90 forward jumps

rejected.name: TASM 2.0 /m (multi-pass)
rejected.why: removes the forward-jump NOPs; both modules mismatch
